source.title: Graded Entity-Familiarity Readouts in Language Models: Polish Adaptation, Cross-Language Robustness, and Refusal Steering

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends activation-direction steering to an entity-familiarity setting and reports its effects on user-facing refusal. It tests whether distinct directions can steer refusal, but not the original harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction or its all-layer ablation.
record.gate_note: The refusal-steering and related refusal-readout results are recorded. The paper's entity-familiarity gradation, language-transfer, and abstention-gating comparisons are not rows because they do not test the listed refusal-direction versions. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study borrows difference-of-means activation steering, citing Arditi et al., and applies it to abstention on unfamiliar entities, an epistemic 'I don't know this person' refusal. It does not study refusal of harmful requests. Neither of its directions is the harmful-minus-harmless direction: one is familiar minus unfamiliar entities, the other refused minus non-refused within unfamiliar entities. It also does no ablation, weight edit, jailbreak or reasoning-model test. Its results describe a related but different behaviour, so they bear on no version and belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that a one-dimensional familiarity direction strongly steers Gemma-4-12B's abstention refusal in both directions, and that a distinct late refusal direction gives an independent, mostly suppressive handle. They stress this shows steering potency, not mediation by the model's natural prompt-time familiarity computation. The refusal in question is abstention on unfamiliar entities, not refusal of harmful requests.
record.recipe_differences: It uses difference-of-means residual-stream directions and activation addition, but the primary direction contrasts familiar with unfamiliar entities rather than harmful with harmless instructions. Steering is at one layer during generation, not ablation at every layer and position; no weight edit is used.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal varies with steering dose and entity condition. The familiarity direction is applied at L30 and the separate refusal direction at L44; the effect is reported on one model and one domain.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-4-12B-it on v1 athletes, adding a rank-one familiarity direction at L30 moves abstention refusal monotonically. Known entities go from 0.24 to 1.00 at α=-24, and unknown-real and fabricated entities go from 0.81 and 0.64 to 0.00 at α=+8. Random equal-norm directions produce no refusals but destroy output coherence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epistemic abstention (refusing to answer about unfamiliar entities) is steerable bidirectionally by a single difference-of-means entity-familiarity direction.

fits_no_version.finding: A late-layer (L44) abstention direction, at cosine -0.14 to the familiarity direction, suppresses abstention refusal (0.64→0.31 and 0.81→0.40 at α=-12). It barely increases refusal and has no effect on known entities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entity-abstention refusal has more than one steerable linear handle: a mid-depth familiarity direction and a distinct, mostly suppressive late refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Natural abstention varies by model and domain. Only Gemma-4 refuses: 0.52–0.64 per answer on real people versus 0.03 on cities. Bielik, Qwen3 and PLLuM give zero refusals in 1,600 answers each.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A model's natural abstention policy can differ from its entity-familiarity readout and vary by domain.

record.problems: The causal steering result is from one model and one domain, and directions are estimated on the same 42 entities per condition used for evaluation. The intervention acts at every generation position, so it does not isolate the prompt-time pathway. The random-direction controls are destructive at the relevant amplitudes, and the degeneration checks do not establish preserved general capability or semantics.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant reported refusal-direction result was omitted.

untested.parts: No harmful-minus-harmless direction is derived, ablated or added. Refusal of harmful requests is not measured.
No weight edit or abliteration is tested.
No jailbreaks are tested, and there is no training against ablation.
There is no test of whether harmful-request refusal is affine, a cone, or a dominant direction plus others. The two directions studied concern entity abstention.
The study separates familiarity from abstention policy, not harmfulness judgment from refusal.
The cross-language results concern familiarity probes, not a refusal direction.
No reasoning models are tested; Qwen3 is run with thinking disabled.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. The study's refusal is knowledge abstention, and neither direction is the harmful-minus-harmless direction. Arditi et al. is cited only as methodological background. The steering results apply to one model and one domain (n=42 per condition), use directions estimated on the evaluation entities, and apply steering at every generation position.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not derive the harmful-minus-harmless instruction refusal direction, ablate it, test removal of refusal, or evaluate general capabilities after ablation. Its intervention uses a familiarity contrast.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No jailbreak attack or training against direction ablation is tested.

The direction comparison is tested only in Gemma-4-12B-it on the v1 athletes set; the study does not test affine or cone descriptions, other models or domains, or whether these directions explain naturally occurring refusal through the prompt-time pathway.
The study distinguishes entity familiarity from abstention behavior, not harmfulness judgment from refusal.
Language-transfer results concern familiarity readouts, not transfer of a refusal direction.
The study does not vary when or how refusal is trained.

rows.note: The paper also reports a zero-leakage probe AUROC of 0.910 for this condition; it does not state an uncertainty interval for that value.
rows.check: This is a correlational readout of entity-abstention refusal from a familiarity score. It is not harmful-request refusal or a refusal direction, so it does not bear on V4. The state is valid only for the study's own measure.
